DIST AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND ADDL.

MACT, RAICHUR,
IN MVC. NO.69/2016, DATED-08.11.2017, BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AS PRAYED FOR AND FIXING THE ENTIRE LIABILITY ON THE RESPONDENT NO.1 TO 3 AND ETC.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The claimants are in appeal against the award of Rs.2,88,443/- and Rs.2,10,952/- respectively granted to them for the injuries that they suffered in an accident which occurred on 20.05.2014.
2. The claimants contend that the accident occurred between the two wheeler in which they were traveling and the tanker lorry.

The police after investigation, had laid a charge sheet against the driver of the tanker and this by itself proved that the cause of the accident was the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the tanker and in the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6898 light of this charge sheet, the Tribunal could not have stated that the rider of the motorcycle had also contributed the extent of 50%.

3. The learned counsel appearing for the insurer however contents that the reasoning of the Tribunal which is based on examination of the spot sketch, cannot be found fault with, especially when it was noticed that the rider of the motorcycle was traveling on the wrong side.
4. In a case of an accident between two vehicles, the best witnesses to state the cause of the accident would be the respective drivers.
In this case, the rider of the motorcycle was examined, as he himself was a claimant in one of the cases and he has asserted that the driver of the tanker lorry was responsible for the accident.
The insurer, on the other hand has not produced any evidence such as the evidence of the lorry driver which should have been the best evidence to rebut this evidence of the claimant.

3 5.

In the light of the fact that there was no evidence on behalf of the lorry driver, the finding of the Tribunal, on NC: 2024:KHC-K:6898 the basis of an examination of the spot sketch could not be justified more so when the police after investigation have formed an opinion that the rider of the tanker lorry alone was responsible.

6. Consequently, the finding of the Tribunal by which it had attributed negligence to an extent of 50% on the claimants is set aside and it is held that the driver of the tanker lorry was completely responsible for the accident and as a result the insurer of this tanker lorry i.e., respondent No.3 would be liable to pay the compensation.
7. As far as the claim for enhancement is concerned, it is noticed that the Tribunal has assessed the disability and also the amount spent towards medical expenses correctly.
Similarly, the amounts awarded under the other heads also are adequate.
8. I am therefore of the view that there is no justification for enhancing the compensation.

Thus,
while affirming the compensation it is held that the insurer- NC: 2024:KHC-K:6898 respondent No.3 would be liable to pay compensation.
To this extent, the award of the tribunal is modified.
The appeals are accordingly allowed in part.
